## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Uttarattheraapadāna* is a Pali verse biography located in the Therāpadāna section of the Khuddaka Nikāya. According to commentary preserved alongside the verse tradition, the text describes the past-life meritorious deeds of the elder Uttara: during the dispensation of the past Buddha Sumedha, he was an accomplished sky-wandering wizard (*vijjādhara*) who beheld the Buddha radiating six-colored light from beneath a forest tree, descended to pay homage, and presented an offering of pure *kaṇikāra* flowers [Patton 2018].

Text-reuse analysis demonstrates extensive sharing of verse material between this work and the rest of Pali literature.
